lines.text: In the hall stands a clock that has never been late, not once. Tick, tick, tick: never faster, never slower.
Music has a clock inside it too
Now, at the piano. Listen to a clock or your own heartbeat. Tap along on your knee without stopping.
And here is how it ended.

A man named Maelzel sold a ticking machine to keep the beat: the metronome. (A Dutchman called Winkel had built it first, but Maelzel’s name was on the box.) Beethoven was one of the first composers to write its numbers on his music.
The clock in the hall would have approved.
One more thing to try. Clap a steady beat while someone counts to twenty. Did you stay with them all the way?
When the clock started again, two strangers were waiting in the hall. One was in a terrible hurry. The other refused to move.
